Way too physical: it's 90% running around and only 10% driving. Constant work, not even 5 minutes to yourself. I take a 30 minute break because I have diabetes and i need to eat but the other drivers don't take a break. Bad weather: When it rains we're outside in it all day and we have to deliver the same amount of packages regardless of how the weather slows us down. The stress of being against the clock and potentially being out until past 9pm. There's many loopholes! Most routes are programmed to be 9 hours long on average but you're 'self employed' so you get to go home whenever you deliver your last parcel. So some days you might finish 2 hours early if you go quick... but the systems' algorithm learns how many parcels you (as a driver) are able deliver per hour... and they will program more parcels into your route next time so that you're still out delivering for the full 9 hours. You are penalised if you bring back packages. Amazon thinks that if they penalize you for bringing back undelivered packages, it means more packages get delivered. But in reality it just encourages drivers to leave parcels on peoples doorsteps or random safe places without permission from the customer. And if the parcel gets stolen or damaged from the weather, we are also penalised. So we can't win. You can only win if the customer is home to take the delivery or if you get away with leaving it in a safe place. 50% of the time, customers aren't home. So you are standing around outside wasting time like a melon. A wet melon if its raining too. A lot of the time you are delivering to multiple addresses in 1 drop. So you might be happy when you realise you only have 110 drops for the day, but a lot of the drops are delivering to a house and 3 of their neighbours. So in reality you're really delivering to 250 separate addresses. You have to urinate in a bottle or a bush, the rumours are true. Doing a poo is a grey area. Nobody talks about that. Ever. Just drive to a nearby pub or something I guess. We all share a fleet of Van's and most of them are damaged from previous drivers.
